source.title: Quality Is Not a Safety Proxy Under Quantization

page_placements.theme: Refusal direction and refusal behaviour under fine-tuning, quantization and uncensoring: drift, compression and dissociation

record.tranche_reason: The study uses refusal-direction geometry as one of four diagnostic probes for identifying dangerous quantized checkpoints, but does not intervene on the direction or test the claimed causal mechanism.
record.gate_note: The study reports cosine similarity to an FP16 refusal direction and whether that geometry separates dangerous quantization rows; these probe results are recorded under fits_no_version because they do not test the causal effects named by the claim. The reported refusal losses under quantization are not rows for these versions: quantization does not manipulate the claimed direction. The safety-associated-neuron quantization-error result is not a test of the single-direction claim.
record.test_reason: The study computes a refusal direction and reports only its cosine similarity to the FP16 direction, as a diagnostic for spotting dangerous quantized checkpoints. It never ablates or adds the direction and never ties it causally to refusal rates. Cosine geometry is a stability measure, a related construct, so it tests no version. The refusal drops under quantization are behavioural changes not produced by manipulating the direction.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that retained quality cannot waive direct safety evaluation for the quantized checkpoints studied. They find the latent probes, including refusal-direction geometry, to be weak or null separators of dangerous rows. The safety-neuron error effect is global, not regime-specific, and is not causal.
record.recipe_differences: The original study uses a difference-in-means direction with causal ablation and addition; this study measures cosine geometry to an FP16 refusal direction as a diagnostic probe and performs no direction intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The refusal-direction geometry probe covers a 17-cell Hugging Face-backed FP16/AWQ/GPTQ subset; the study reports no detectable RTSI association or danger-regime separation in that subset.

fits_no_version.finding: The refusal direction stays geometrically intact under AWQ/GPTQ quantization (cosine > 0.97 in every cell), yet behavioural refusal falls 12–68 pp in hidden-danger rows.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preserved refusal-direction geometry under quantization does not guarantee preserved refusal behaviour.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-direction cosine has no detectable association with the RTSI screen (r = −0.144, p = 0.673, n = 17) and does not separate danger regimes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-direction cosine to the FP16 direction is not a usable screen for refusal loss under quantization.

record.code_released: not stated (public URLs are omitted during review; review artifacts are supplied through the conference supplementary-material channel)
record.problems: The refusal-direction probe is descriptive rather than causal and covers only 17 cells. The paper notes limited model and family coverage, LLM judges rather than human adjudication, and a scoped single-turn safety battery.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for the claim versions were reported. The paper’s quantization refusal-loss rows and safety-associated-neuron quantization-error result were left out because they do not manipulate or directly test the claimed single-direction mechanism.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of the direction; no test of mediation or of preserved capabilities.
No attack analysis tied to the direction; no adversarial training.
No comparison of one direction against several.
Harm judgment and refusal are not separated.
No causal transfer of the direction across languages or variants. Only cosine stability across quantized variants is reported.

record.verdict_notes: Keeping T4/uses_without_test is defensible, though T6 would also fit: the direction is only a descriptive probe. The direction-preserved-but-refusal-drops pattern echoes prior work the paper cites (refs [1], [4]). Without an intervention it cannot challenge V1. The models are small (1B–7B) and judged by LLM judges.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not ablate or add the difference-in-means direction, test whether it mediates refusal, or assess preservation of other abilities after such an intervention.
No direction ablation is converted into a weight edit or evaluated as abliteration.
No attack is tested for suppressing the direction, and no training against its ablation is evaluated.
The study does not compare a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account of refusal.
The study does not test whether harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are separately encoded.
The study does not test transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
The study does not vary refusal-training methods or timing.
The study does not evaluate reasoning models.

relation.reason: The refusal direction is used as one of four latent probes for spotting dangerous quantized rows. Its mediation of refusal is never tested.

tranche.reason: The study computes a refusal direction only as a diagnostic probe. It reports cosine stability to the FP16 direction and its correlation with the study's own RTSI screen, with no ablation, addition or causal link to refusal rates. That is a stability measure, not a test of any version.

source_check.notes: The text never states how the refusal direction is computed (method, layer, prompt sets) and gives no per-cell cosines. The cosine-stable/refusal-drop pattern touches V6 (transfer across quantized variants) and V1 only at the level of geometry, so it fits no version. The authors' 'not causal' wording is softer than the record's: the effect 'does not establish a causal mechanism'.

statements.correction: Suggested wording: 'no detectable association with RTSI at this sample size (r = −0.144, p = 0.673, n = 17)'. Hidden-danger AWQ/GPTQ refusal deltas: −12.27 (mistral-7b GPTQ) to −68.18 (llama3.2-1b GPTQ) pp.
statements.problem: Numbers and conditions are right. Cosine >0.97 holds in every quantized (AWQ/GPTQ) cell of the 17-cell HF subset. Direct-refusal losses in hidden-danger rows run 12.27-68.18 pp (Table 1). 'No association' slightly overstates the source: the text says no *detectable* association at this sample size.
